one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent introduced 64-bit and 16-bit overlapping reads on top of a correct 32-bit extraction baseline, producing non-4-byte-aligned addresses and incorrect values, then declared success after only verifying JSON format and integer type rather than comparing against the reference output.
t_err_evidence: attempting to extend extraction logic to include 64-bit reads
t_commit_evidence: Step 22: the agent successfully adds a 16-bit read loop alongside the 64-bit loop, resulting in the final wrong mixed-width extraction state (1396 entries with non-aligned keys at 0,2,4,6,...) that is never corrected before completion at step 32.
trigger_explanation: After the agent had a nearly-correct 32-bit extraction (698 values after fixing zero-filtering at step 13), it adopted the false premise that adding 64-bit reads would increase meaningful coverage, without checking whether the reference output uses only strict 32-bit little-endian word extraction. This unverified assumption drove the agent to introduce conflicting multi-width reads that corrupted address alignment and value accuracy.
forewarning_evidence: No replacement was performed, old_str ... did not appear verbatim in /app/extract.js.
